objective: metric round 10: the ledger of refuted constructions is in the prompt

metrics.title: Rank fidelity of the SID prefix tree, realised as a geodesic tree of hyperbolic Frechet barycentres in the frozen reference Poincare ball, to the reference distances over all training pairs.
metrics.formula:
Fix curvature c = 1 (the curvature of the frozen reference ball, as stated by the reference; not fitted). Let x_i be the reference SOURCE representation of item i, already in the unit Poincare ball B_c = {x : sqrt(c)||x|| < 1}.
Mobius addition: u (+) v = ((1 + 2c<u,v> + c||v||^2) u + (1 - c||u||^2) v) / (1 + 2c<u,v> + c^2||u||^2||v||^2).
Poincare distance: d(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c) * ||(-u)(+)v|| ).
Origin maps: log_0(x) = artanh(sqrt(c)||x||) x / (sqrt(c)||x||); exp_0(w) = tanh(sqrt(c)||w||) w / (sqrt(c)||w||), with exp_0(0)=0.
FRE(S) = hyperbolic Frechet (Karcher) mean of a set S: initialise b = exp_0( mean_{x in S} log_0(x) ), then repeat 60 times: b <- exp_b( (1/2) * mean_{x in S} log_b(x) ), where log_b(y) = log_0( (-b)(+)y ) / (1 - c||b||^2). The step 1/2 and the 60 sweeps are a fixed numerical schedule, not a tuned parameter.
For item i and level l = 1..L: A_l(i) = the level-l prefix cell of i; p_l(i) = FRE({ x_j : A_l(j) = A_l(i) }), one barycentre per cell, reused by all its members.
SID-induced distance: D(i,j) = sum_{l=1}^{L} d( p_l(i), p_l(j) ). D(i,j) = 0 iff i and j agree at every level.
Reference distance: R(i,j) = d( x_i, x_j ).
score = Spearman rank correlation between {D(i,j)} and {R(i,j)} over the pair set P.
P = 200000 distinct unordered pairs (i<j) of training-split items, drawn uniformly by numpy.random.default_rng(0) over the sorted list of training item indices. The seed and the size are a compute budget held fixed for every table, never tuned against a recall.
Return score. It lies in [-1, +1]; higher is better.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table, the integer code per item per level; (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference, namely the source representation x_i per item and the training-split item list. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 run.
metrics.geometry: everything lives in a ball of fixed negative curvature c = 1. The curvature enters in exactly two places and nowhere else. (a) Every cell is summarised by a Frechet barycentre computed with hyperbolic log/exp maps and Poincare distances, so a cell's representative is the least-squares centre in the ball, not a coordinate-wise average. (b) The SID distance is a sum of Poincare distances between those barycentres, i.e. the prefix trie is realised as a geodesic tree inside the ball. This is the right realisation because a prefix hierarchy is a tree and hyperbolic space is the space that embeds trees with bounded distortion at curvature matched to the tree's branching. At c -> 0 the barycentres collapse to Euclidean means, the Poincare distance collapses to half the Euclidean distance, and the score degenerates into a linear-projection score; that degeneration is exactly what the curvature is there to prevent, so the comparison is only meaningful because of the map.
metrics.why: Recall@10 is a rank question over all pairs, not over one anchor. A table can only retrieve item i with a 10-candidate prefix probe if its cells are the cells of the reference geometry. Q_H scores one canonical prefix contrast; HBAA scores one anchor point against a mean of ten negatives. This metric scores the entire hierarchy against the entire item cloud at once, over roughly two hundred thousand pairs, and it is invariant to which single item is treated as the query: it asks whether the SID table is a low-distortion hyperbolic summary of the reference ball, which is precisely the property an index needs for 10-cell probes to suffice. It also uses the deepest levels without the level-2/3 collapse that sinks Q_H: a level-l cell contributes only the geodesic spread of its own barycentre, which shrinks to zero as that cell becomes a single item, so an over-split finish earns nothing while a semantically coherent deep level still adds resolution. Nothing here is a rearrangement of a single anchor's margin, likelihood or coverage; it is a global isometry score over the full pair structure.
metrics.compute: per-cell barycentres computed once: sum over cells of (n_cell x 60 x 2) log/exp-map evaluations, about 24587 * 60 * 2 is roughly 3e6 map evaluations, plus one L-depth pass to assign p_l(i); then 2e5 pairs x L <= 4 Poincare distances, about 1e6 vectorised operations. Under 10 s on a single core for 24587 items and 256 codes, well inside the one-minute budget.
metrics.risks: (a) saturation: if the reference's own pair distances are dominated by one large-scale gradient, most plausible tables land in a narrow 0.2-0.4 band and the Spearman against recall is noisy; (b) unbalanced cell sizes: a few huge level-1 cells can dominate the barycentres and make several levels' contributions nearly identical, wasting the ladder; (c) the pair sample is fixed, so its sampling variance is not averaged away across corpora; (d) if the frozen reference representations are nearly rank-1 (collapsed during their own training) the Poincare distances become a monotone rescaling of a scalar and the coherence signal disappears.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on a table whose level-1 codes are semantically scrambled while its trie is perfectly balanced, for example codes assigned by an item-id hash: all barycentres then sit near the ball's origin, the Poincare distances between them are small and nearly constant, D is nearly constant and the Spearman falls to 0. It is equally 0 on the pathological table with 24587 distinct level-1 codes (D constant) and on the one-code table (D identically 0, correlation undefined, scored 0), so neither collapse nor total splitting is ever rewarded.

metrics.title: Curvature-normalised Gromov common-ancestor expected rank of the target over the items its own level-1 cell fails to absorb.
metrics.formula: Let N be the item count, K the number of distinct level-1 codes in the exported table, c = c_ref > 0 the frozen reference curvature, tau = tau_ref > 0 its frozen temperature, o = 0 the ball origin. For every item h let s_h be the reference source vector and t_h its target vector; map to the Poincare ball B_c = {x : c||x||^2 < 1} by x_h = exp_0^c(s_h), y_h = exp_0^c(t_h) (identity if the reference already emits ball points). Poincare distance: d_c(x,y) = c^{-1/2} arcosh( 1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)) ). Gromov product (common-ancestor similarity) about o: G_c(x,y) = (x|y)_o = 1/2 [ d_c(o,x) + d_c(o,y) - d_c(x,y) ]. For item i let H_i be the set of items occurring before i in the TRAINING split (its history, i excluded), and q_i = Frechet barycentre of {x_h : h in H_i} in B_c, q_i = argmin_{q in B_c} sum_{h in H_i} d_c(q,x_h)^2, computed by the standard Riemannian iteration: initialise q = x_{last history item}; repeat 20 times { u = |H_i|^{-1} sum_{h in H_i} log^c_q(x_h); q <- exp^c_q(u); stop if ||u|| < 1e-6 } with the Poincare exp/log. Let code1(j) be the level-1 integer code of j, C_i = {j : code1(j) = code1(i)}, M_i = N - |C_i|. Define positive logit a_i = exp( G_c(q_i, y_i) / tau ) and negative mass D_i = sum_{j not in C_i} exp( G_c(q_i, y_j) / tau ). Then p_i = a_i / (a_i + D_i) and lift_i = ln( (M_i + 1) p_i ). METRIC = (1/|Q|) sum_{i in Q} lift_i, with Q = { i : H_i nonempty and M_i >= 1 }; if K = 1 or Q empty the metric is exactly 0. Higher is better. c and tau are the reference's own frozen constants; M_i and K come from the table; the iteration counts are fixed algorithm settings, not fitted to any recall.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (level-1 integer code per item); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (source vector s_h, target vector t_h per item, plus c_ref and tau_ref); and the TRAINING split (only to build H_i). Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: the score is built from the Gromov product, a genuinely hyperbolic similarity: (x|y)_o equals the distance from o to the geodesic joining x and y, i.e. the depth of their common ancestor in the reference's tree. It is defined only through the negative-curvature metric and has no Euclidean counterpart (a flat space has no common-ancestor invariant). The query is a Frechet barycentre, a curved mean defined only through the exp/log maps; curvature -c enters the distance, the barycentre and G. The comparison is meaningful precisely because the space is negatively curved.
metrics.why: Stage 3 recalls the target by following the code tree from a query built from the user history. A good level-1 cell is exactly the set of items geometrically confusable with the target (the deep common-ancestor neighbours of the history). Removing that cell from the candidate pool must leave the target as the dominant Gromov match, so lift_i is large when the cell absorbed the hard negatives and drops toward 0 when those hard negatives remain outside. Averaged over Q this is a retrieval-quality proxy that varies with the table's partition. Over Q_H it adds: Q_H ranks the target prefix from one fixed query and ignores the geometry of the confusables; here the full history is a curved query point, the positive is scored against the entire off-cell distribution (not a mean of ten), and the Gromov product measures subtree overlap rather than raw proximity. Over HBAA it adds: HBAA averages the negative side into one barycentre and uses a single distance contrast; here the negative side is the whole table-defined off-cell distribution under a temperatured softmax (a true expected rank), so hard negatives are not averaged away, the partition itself defines the pool, and the uniform size-matched null (M_i + 1) keeps collapse neutral instead of rewarding it.
metrics.compute: per query the metric needs d_c to every off-cell item, so O(|Q| N) distances. With |Q| <= N = 24587 and N = 24587 this is at most 6.0e8 Poincare distances; chunked over 512 queries in float32, with c||y_j||^2 and d_c(o,y_j) precomputed, that is about 25-45 s on one CPU core. The Frechet barycentres add O(|Q| mean|H| 20) ~ 1.5e7 operations. If a slower machine is used, queries are stride-subsampled to at most 8K = 2048 items (a constant derived from the codebook size K = 256, never from a recall), cutting the distance count to 5e7 (<10 s) with a mean shift below 0.01. Nothing is trained and no matrix is persisted.
metrics.risks: (i) the metric depends on the frozen reference's geometry, so it is a property of table-plus-reference, not of the integer codes alone; here the reference is frozen, which is intended. (ii) Near-singleton cells give M_i ~ N for all i, so every lift is near 0 and the ordering is carried by small residuals; variance across tables shrinks. (iii) A norm prior is present because G_c contains d_c(o,y_j); if the reference pushes all items onto the boundary, that term dominates and the metric degenerates toward a norm ranking. (iv) arcosh arguments must be clamped to >= 1 or x = y produces NaNs. (v) The metric is invariant to relabelling of codes (only the partition matters), which is intentional, but it means two tables with the same partition but different code order score identically.
metrics.failure_mode: it must be worst on a table whose level-1 partition is anti-aligned with the reference geometry - e.g. codes assigned by an item-id hash, by a random frequency bucket, or by deliberately grouping far items and isolating each item from its Gromov neighbours. Then for every i the target's deep-ancestor confusables lie outside C_i, D_i is dominated by them, p_i ~ 1/(M_i + 1), and lift_i ~ 0 (or strongly negative if the cell is anti-correlated), so METRIC ~ 0 regardless of K. The one-code table is exactly 0 by construction, and a random relabelling of a fine partition leaves the metric unchanged, also ~0 because the cell no longer absorbs the confusables.

metrics.title: Cross-fitted full-negative expected-rank of the level-1 bucket, queried by the geodesic barycentre of the user's whole training history.
metrics.formula:
Work in the frozen reference's ball rescaled to unit curvature (c=1) by x -> sqrt(c_ref)*x; this is a fixed isometry, not a parameter. Let d(.,.) be that Poincare geodesic distance, and let Bary(S) be the Karcher/Frechet barycentre of a finite set S in the ball (the point minimising the sum of squared d). Let b(i) be the level-1 SID code of item i, and let the frozen reference give a source point s_i and a target point t_i per item (same ball).
Split the TRAINING users deterministically by hash(u) mod 2 into folds A and B. For direction A->B let T_A be all training items of fold-A users and let C_A = number of distinct level-1 codes present in T_A. Define, for every code b, mu_b = Bary({ t_i : i in T_A, b(i)=b }) (origin if empty). For each fold-B user u with non-empty training history H_u, using only items before u's final training item i+_u, set q_u = Bary({ s_j : j in H_u }) and p = b(i+_u). Define
  R_u = sum_{b != p, b in T_A} sigma( (d(q_u,mu_p)^2 - d(q_u,mu_b)^2) / (2*tau^2) ),
with sigma(z)=1/(1+e^-z) and tau = tau_ref, the frozen reference's contrastive temperature (rescaled with the ball; no grid, no tuning). Set e_u = R_u/(C_A-1).
Size-matched null: let n_b = |{i in T_A : b(i)=b}|. Sort T_A by the stable key CRC32(str(item_id)) ascending and hand out the codes in descending-n_b order in contiguous blocks of the observed sizes n_b; call this assignment btilde(i). Define mu_b^null = Bary({ t_i : i in T_A, btilde(i)=b }) and R_u^null, e_u^null exactly as above with mu^null. Then
  M = (1/|P|) * sum_{u in P} ( e_u^null - e_u ),
pooling the B->A direction (symmetric, centroids from fold B, users from fold A); |P| = number of evaluated training users. C_A=1 gives M=0. Higher M is better (range about [-1,+1]; perfect partition -> e_obs ~ 0, e_null ~ 0.5, so M -> +0.5; no-information or collapsed table -> e_obs = e_null -> 0; anti-aligned table -> M < 0).
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (integer level-1 code per item; deeper levels unused); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (per-item source s_i and target t_i, its curvature c_ref and temperature tau_ref, all fitted on training pairs only); the TRAINING interaction split with timestamps (to form H_u and i+_u). Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: the number is built entirely from the Poincare geodesic distance d (arcosh form) in a ball of fixed negative curvature, from Karcher/Frechet barycentres (whose defining iteration uses exp/log maps and parallel transport along geodesics, so it is not a Euclidean mean), and from squared-geodesic margins. Curvature enters in d and in every barycentre, and c_ref fixes the unit rescaling; the whole construction is meaningless in a flat space because the Karcher mean, the log/exp maps and the geodesic margin all change.
metrics.why: with ~24587 items and ~256 level-1 codes a bucket holds ~96 items, so Recall@10 is high essentially only when the positive's bucket is ranked at or near the top of the competing buckets; the soft expected rank R_u is exactly that rank, averaged over the full set of 256 alternative buckets rather than a ten-negative mean. The query is the geodesic barycentre of the user's whole history, so the score asks where the user's trajectory points in the reference's source->target geometry. Against Q_H it adds the learned cross-space behaviour geometry (Q_H only counts prefix agreement and is blind to where the history points); against HBAA it replaces the mean of ten negatives by the full negative-bucket distribution with a logistic margin, so one hard competing bucket that would displace the positive from the top-10 is visible instead of being averaged away; the cross-fitting removes self-inclusion and the deterministic size-matched null removes the code-count/collapse advantage that destroyed the path-likelihood metric.
metrics.compute: 2 folds x (256 Karcher means over ~50-100 points, ~10 iterations) + one history barycentre per evaluated user (~a few thousand) + |P| x 256 vectorised geodesic evaluations x 2 (observed and null), about 10-30 million flops; seconds to well under a minute on 24587 items and 256 codes.
metrics.risks: if the reference's source and target live in separate non-comparable spaces the score is undefined (require shared ball); a near-chance reference makes q_u and mu_b uninformative and M noise around 0; tables with very few non-empty level-1 codes give high-variance M (the null centres it at 0 but does not shrink the variance); very short histories send q_u to the origin and reduce the metric to a global prior; item_id hashes must be used for the null order so raw id/popularity order cannot leak structure.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on a table whose level-1 codes are assigned by a criterion orthogonal or anti-aligned to the frozen source->target geometry while keeping the same code count and bucket sizes (e.g. level-1 = popularity decile or a hash of item id), where e_obs ~ e_null ~ 0.5 and M ~ 0, and most negative when buckets deliberately group behaviourally distant items and split behaviourally close ones (e_obs > e_null); the one-code table gives exactly 0 by construction.
